clue.text: For example, Clementine's father's free ferry to inn

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose and allowed to settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about a girl's dad, who was apparently free to ferry people to an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges FERRYTOINN. The definition alludes to the American folk song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine', whose father was 'a miner, forty-niner'. The 's after father stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk song, Clementine's father was a gold prospector of the 1849 California rush, one example of such a man.

clue.text: Assemble on account of harvest

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in 'praised for his courage'
to harvest crops is to gather them in

explanation.surface: People come together because the crops are being brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned verb for meeting together as a group, a synonym of assemble.

clue.text: Unchecked, rave about hi-fi item

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to rave is to rant wildly
an amplifier, or amp, is part of a hi-fi system

explanation.surface: Someone raving uncontrollably about a piece of stereo equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchecked spreads without restraint, as weeds or inflation run wild.

clue.text: Painting giving small number shock in church

parts.note: No. is the short form of number

indicators.note: in places the shock inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a sudden fright, as in 'gave me quite a turn'

explanation.surface: A painting that shocks a small congregation at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gave me a turn' is a British idiom for a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler called his dreamy night scenes nocturnes, so the word names a kind of painting as well as a musical piece.

clue.text: Male inhabitant of Cumbria or Iceland?

definitions.text: Male inhabitant of Cumbria or Iceland?

parts.words: Male inhabitant of Cumbria or Iceland?
parts.note: Cumbria lies in the north of England, and Iceland is literally a northern nation, so a man from either fits the phrase

explanation.surface: A question about what to call a man from Cumbria or Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in England's far north-west; the question mark flags the playful second reading for Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the north of England is a northerner in this sense; Iceland is a country in the north, taken literally.

clue.text: French writer popular in Derby, for example

indicators.note: in tells us to set popular inside the race

parts.note: the Derby is a famous English horse race run at Epsom
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A French author who is well liked in the English city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby reads as the Midlands city, but it is the Epsom horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French dramatist, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Bound, just before the end, to get the point

indicators.note: stopping just before the end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to caper is to leap or bound about playfully

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up just before finishing so as to make their point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Expresses glee over mesh around son's lookout post

parts.note: to crow is to exult or express glee

indicators.note: around puts the net about the son

parts.note: a net is a mesh
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father gloats about catching his son in a net at the lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Fall headlong from fruit-tree encountered

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles out of a fruit tree they came upon.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to drop steeply and fast, as a stone falls.

clue.text: Half record's backing by Italian fantasist

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome

indicators.note: backing means the half of the word is read in reverse
half takes the first three of the six letters of record

explanation.surface: Half a record company's financial backing comes from an Italian dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes REC from record and 'backing' turns it to CER, placed beside ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer is one who invents fanciful stories, a fantasist.

clue.text: Greek tragedians first to celebrate sun-god

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of celebrate

parts.note: Horus was an Egyptian sky and sun god

explanation.surface: Greek playwrights are the first to honour the sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy the chorus was a group of performers commenting on the action, so the plural fits.

clue.text: US state only briefly identified, unfortunately

indicators.note: naming the state only briefly means its last letters are cut off

parts.note: Alaska is a US state

explanation.surface: A US state was named only in passing, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, much like sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Not generous, to let go of part only

parts.note: to unhand someone is to release them from one's grip
some means a part, not the whole

explanation.surface: A mean person lets go of only part of what they hold.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of unhandsome is mean or ungracious, the opposite of a handsome gift.

clue.text: Old 'South African's stolen books about wine

indicators.note: about places the stolen books around the wine

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A South African of old has stolen books on the subject of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT goes between HOT and OT. The 's after African stands for 'has'. The quotation marks show the term is dated and now offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottentot is an old, now offensive, name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.

clue.text: Vessel designed largely for private use?

definitions.text: Vessel designed largely for private use?

parts.words: Vessel designed largely for private use?
parts.note: suggests a personal yacht, but private means an army private, so the ship carries soldiers

explanation.surface: A boat built mainly for one person's own use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like personal; it is the lowest army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship built to carry soldiers, who are largely privates.

clue.text: Greek character escorted back to Athens, originally

indicators.note: back means the word for escorted is read in reverse

parts.note: led means escorted

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A Greek person was escorted back to Athens at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: George has given gold to one involved in conspiracy

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: involved in puts one inside the conspiracy

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man named George has handed gold to a conspirator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' was RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang nicknamed the automatic pilot George, so the name stands for it.

clue.text: Body once incorporated in Lancaster?

parts.note: reads like a company once registered in the town, but the Lancaster was a WWII bomber and its body is the main airframe

explanation.surface: A firm that was once incorporated in the town of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster suggests the English city; it is the RAF's wartime Avro Lancaster bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aircraft, to which wings and tail attach.

clue.text: Element creating trouble in one of the services

indicators.note: in places the trouble inside the service

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Something causing trouble in one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gas, a chemical element.

clue.text: Resolute drivers not disheartened about barrier

indicators.note: about puts these letters around the barrier

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation for drivers
a dam is a barrier across water

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, the middle letter, of the word not

explanation.surface: Determined motorists are not discouraged by a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists or golf clubs; in British crosswords it is usually the AA, the motoring organisation. 'disheartened' makes NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unshakeable in purpose, a synonym of resolute.

clue.text: A new French night worker, one with regular income

parts.note: nuit is French for night
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A new French night-shift worker who earns a steady wage.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant receives an annuity, a fixed yearly payment.

clue.text: A research room a graduate built in Birmingham area

parts.note: a lab is a room for research
taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A laboratory and a graduate are set up in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham suggests the English city, but there is a large Birmingham in Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state Alabama contains the city of Birmingham, so it is the wider area around it.

clue.text: Drum giving rise to a couple of witty sayings

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters reverse
a couple of means the word is taken twice

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, so two of them supply the pair

explanation.surface: A drumbeat that inspires a few witticisms.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall drum beaten with the hands or sticks.

clue.text: Check series of lectures touching feature of building

parts.note: to damp is to check or restrain
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Checking a lecture series that touches on architectural features.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp course is a waterproof layer laid in a wall to stop rising damp.

clue.text: Show amazement, but understand right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: to grasp is to understand

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished but catches on immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as at once; here it means remove R.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw a sharp breath in surprise.

clue.text: Prestige long recognised in court

indicators.note: in places the longing inside the court

parts.note: to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: Prestige that has long been recognised in a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means distinction or prestige.

clue.text: Food item prepared by yours truly at dance

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
taken as written
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dish the speaker made at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a small ball of minced meat, a food item.

clue.text: Possibly the organist's principal halting-place

definitions.meaning: the Principal is a particular organ register, an example of a lever the organist pulls
a place where a bus or train halts

explanation.definitionFit: An organ's sets of pipes are each controlled by a knob of this name, and the same word is a place where vehicles halt.

clue.text: Valet's right to keep vehicle by minister's house

parts.note: a manse is a minister's house, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: to keep puts the vehicle inside

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A valet is entitled to park a van by the minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a male personal servant.
